585	/****************************************************************************
586	 * Network device driver functions
587	 *
588	 * These functions are used by a network device driver for interacting
589	 * with the NuttX network.
590	 *
591	 * Process an incoming IP packet.
592	 *
593	 * This function should be called when the device driver has received
594	 * a packet from the network. The packet from the device driver must
595	 * be present in the d_buf buffer, and the length of the packet
596	 * should be placed in the d_len field.
597	 *
598	 * When the function returns, there may be an outbound packet placed
599	 * in the d_buf packet buffer. If so, the d_len field is set to
600	 * the length of the packet. If no packet is to be sent out, the
601	 * d_len field is set to 0.
602	 *
603	 * The usual way of calling the function is presented by the source
604	 * code below.
605	 *
606	 *     dev->d_len = devicedriver_poll();
607	 *     if (dev->d_len > 0)
608	 *       {
609	 *         ipv4_input(dev);
610	 *         if (dev->d_len > 0)
611	 *           {
612	 *             devicedriver_send();
613	 *           }
614	 *       }

616	 * Note: If you are writing a network device driver that needs ARP
617	 * (Address Resolution Protocol), e.g., when running the network over
618	 * Ethernet, you will need to call the network ARP code before calling
619	 * this function:
620	 *
621	 *     dev->d_len = ethernet_devicedrver_poll();
622	 *     if (dev->d_len > 0)
623	 *       {
624	 *         if (ETHBUF->type == HTONS(ETHTYPE_IP))
625	 *           {
626	 *             arp_ipin();
627	 *             ipv4_input(dev);
628	 *             if (dev->d_len > 0)
629	 *               {
630	 *                 arp_out();
631	 *                 devicedriver_send();
632	 *               }
633	 *           }
634	 *         else if (ETHBUF->type == HTONS(ETHTYPE_ARP))
635	 *           {
636	 *             arp_input();
637	 *             if (dev->d_len > 0)
638	 *               {
639	 *                 devicedriver_send();
640	 *               }
641	 *           }

697	/****************************************************************************
698	 * Polling of connections
699	 *
700	 * These functions will traverse each active network connection structure
701	 * and perform appropriate operations:  devif_poll() will perform TCP
702	 * and UDP polling operations. devif_poll() may be called asynchronously
703	 * from the network driver can accept another outgoing packet.
704	 *
705	 * In both cases, these functions will call the provided callback function
706	 * for every active connection. Polling will continue until all connections
707	 * have been polled or until the user-supplied function returns a non-zero
708	 * value (which it should do only if it cannot accept further write data).
709	 *
710	 * When the callback function is called, there may be an outbound packet
711	 * waiting for service in the device packet buffer, and if so the d_len field
712	 * is set to a value larger than zero. The device driver should then send
713	 * out the packet.
714	 *
715	 * Example:
716	 *   int driver_callback(FAR struct net_driver_s *dev)
717	 *   {
718	 *     if (dev->d_len > 0)
719	 *       {
720	 *         devicedriver_send();
721	 *         return 1; <-- Terminates polling if necessary
722	 *       }
723	 *     return 0;
724	 *   }
725	 *
726	 *   ...
727	 *   devif_poll(dev, driver_callback);
728	 *
729	 * Note: If you are writing a network device driver that needs ARP (Address
730	 * Resolution Protocol), e.g., when running the networ over Ethernet, you
731	 * will need to call the arp_out() function in the callback function
732	 * before sending the packet:
733	 *
734	 *   int driver_callback(FAR struct net_driver_s *dev)
735	 *   {
736	 *     if (dev->d_len > 0)
737	 *       {
738	 *         arp_out();
739	 *         devicedriver_send();
740	 *         return 1; <-- Terminates polling if necessary
741	 *       }
742	 *
743	 *     return 0;
744	 *   }
745	 *
746	 *   Compatible with all old flat buffer NICs
747	 *
748	 *                 tcp_poll()/udp_poll()/pkt_poll()/...(l3/l4)
749	 *                            /              \
750	 *                           /                \
751	 * devif_poll_[l3/l4]_connections()     devif_iob_send() (nocopy:udp/icmp/..)
752	 *            /                                   \      (copy:tcp)
753	 *           /                                     \
754	 *   devif_iob_poll(devif_poll_callback())  devif_poll_callback()
755	 *        /                                           \
756	 *       /                                             \
757	 *  devif_poll("NIC"_txpoll)                     "NIC"_send()(dev->d_buf)
758	 *
759	 ****************************************************************************/
760	
761	int devif_poll(FAR struct net_driver_s *dev, devif_poll_callback_t callback);

763	/****************************************************************************
764	 * Name: neighbor_out
765	 *
766	 * Description:
767	 *   This function should be called before sending out an IPv6 packet. The
768	 *   function checks the destination IPv6 address of the IPv6 packet to see
769	 *   what L2 address that should be used as a destination L2 address.
770	 *
771	 *   If the destination IPv6 address is in the local network (determined
772	 *   by logical ANDing of netmask and our IPv6 address), the function
773	 *   checks the Neighbor Table to see if an entry for the destination IPv6
774	 *   address is found.  If so, an L2 header is pre-pended at the beginning
775	 *   of the packet and the function returns.
776	 *

585	/****************************************************************************
586	 * Network device driver functions
587	 *
588	 * These functions are used by a network device driver for interacting
589	 * with the NuttX network.
590	 *
591	 * Process an incoming IP packet.
592	 *
593	 * This function should be called when the device driver has received
594	 * a packet from the network. The packet from the device driver must
595	 * be present in the d_buf buffer, and the length of the packet
596	 * should be placed in the d_len field.
597	 *
598	 * When the function returns, there may be an outbound packet placed
599	 * in the d_buf packet buffer. If so, the d_len field is set to
600	 * the length of the packet. If no packet is to be sent out, the
601	 * d_len field is set to 0.
602	 *
603	 * The usual way of calling the function is presented by the source
604	 * code below.
605	 *
606	 *     dev->d_len = devicedriver_poll();
607	 *     if (dev->d_len > 0)
608	 *       {
609	 *         ipv4_input(dev);
610	 *         if (dev->d_len > 0)
611	 *           {
612	 *             devicedriver_send();
613	 *           }
614	 *       }
615	 *
616	 * Note: If you are writing a network device driver that needs ARP
617	 * (Address Resolution Protocol), e.g., when running the network over
618	 * Ethernet, you will need to call the network ARP code before calling
619	 * this function:
620	 *
621	 *     dev->d_len = ethernet_devicedrver_poll();
622	 *     if (dev->d_len > 0)
623	 *       {
624	 *         if (ETHBUF->type == HTONS(ETHTYPE_IP))
625	 *           {
626	 *             arp_ipin();
627	 *             ipv4_input(dev);
628	 *             if (dev->d_len > 0)
629	 *               {
630	 *                 arp_out();
631	 *                 devicedriver_send();
632	 *               }
633	 *           }
634	 *         else if (ETHBUF->type == HTONS(ETHTYPE_ARP))
635	 *           {
636	 *             arp_input();
637	 *             if (dev->d_len > 0)
638	 *               {
639	 *                 devicedriver_send();
640	 *               }
641	 *           }
642	 *
643	 ****************************************************************************/
